summary: Count nodes that are not smaller than any value on the path from the root to them.
mainInsight: Carry the maximum value seen so far down the path; a node is good iff its value is at least that maximum. One preorder traversal does it.

approaches.name: Check the whole path for each node
DFS carrying the path maximum
approaches.summary: Pass max_so_far; count when val >= it; update the max.

promptVariants: What state should DFS pass down to decide whether a node is 'good'?
Which pattern is Count Good Nodes?
options: The maximum value on the path from the root
The depth of the node from the root of the tree
The sum of all values on the path from the root
The number of children each node on the path has
cards.answer: The maximum value on the path from the root
cards.explanation: A node is good iff no ancestor is larger, i.e. node.val >= path maximum.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The sum of all values on the path from t: The sum does not decide goodness.

promptVariants: Why is it enough to remember only the maximum of the path?
Why does updating the max before checking still count the node correctly?
cards.answer: A node is good iff its value >= every value on the path, which is equivalent to value >= the path maximum. Updating max_so_far = max(old, val) first and then checking val >= max_so_far is the same as val >= old max, since val >= max(old, val) iff val >= old.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Recursion stack space: ___
Why is `dfs(root, root.val)` started with root.val as the initial maximum?
What does the update `big = max(big, root.val)` before the comparison do?
cards.answer: Starting with the root's own value makes the root good (it is >= itself). After updating big to include the current node, `root.val >= big` holds exactly when the node is at least as large as every ancestor; the updated big is then passed to the children.
keyPoints: val >= big after updating == val >= old max
cards.explanation: -inf as the initial maximum also works.

promptVariants: How many good nodes are in the chain 3 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 (each the left child of the previous)?
cards.explanation: 3 (root) and 4 are not smaller than their ancestors; 1 and the last 3 (< 4) are not good. (2: 3 and 4)
